Subject: Air-gapped artifact push: repository handoff and rollback window

Hi Tim —

Following up from last week's call with the ACME infra team. We're preparing to push the signed runtime artifacts and container images into your on-prem artifactory for the air-gapped activation. High level plan below; attachments include a manifest (artifact-manifest.yml) and a short signing-instructions.pdf for the operator.

Planned maintenance window (requested):
- UTC: 2028-10-09 01:00 — 03:00 (2 hours)
- Local (PDT): 2028-10-08 18:00 — 20:00

What we will do in the window:
1) Hand off a single tarball containing: signed-image.bundle, manifest, checksums, and operator install script.
2) Operator validates signatures and digests (we provide cosign/openssl instructions).
3) Staged activation on a single node; smoke test; then rollout to remaining nodes with 5-min pauses.
4) If any test fails, we revert to the prior image and record a rollback ticket (INFRA-4521).

Key asks from ACME side before the push:
- Confirm acceptance of the proposed window or suggest an alternative.
- Confirm the egress / package import path: will you accept a physical media drop (SFTP from carrier) or SCP from our isolated upload host?
- Provide the operator contact and public key fingerprint (for encrypted handoff) or confirm you want us to use the ephemeral envelope key in the manifest.

Attachments in this message: artifact-manifest.yml (contains artifact list + digests), signing-instructions.pdf (operator validation steps). Full digest file will be published in the push message.

If useful, we can run a dry-run verification (no activation) a day ahead to confirm operator verification and checksum validation.

Thanks —
David Kim
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

David —

Thanks for the plan, this looks thorough. A few clarifying questions before we lock the window: 

1) Verification: will you provide both SHA256 digests and an RSA signature (we prefer two independent verifiers)? We need to ensure signatures can be validated in our FIPS-enabled environment.
2) Key rotation & provenance: what's the expected lifetime of the envelope key in the manifest? Do you rotate signing keys per release?
3) Transport: we prefer a physical media drop into our locked staging SFTP box (no direct inbound SCP). Can you confirm the package format (tar.gz vs zip)? Also, we require an MD5 for legacy tooling in addition to SHA256 for compatibility.
4) Rollback: please provide the exact commands/operators will run to revert to the previous image (we keep an immutable snapshot of the current rootfs).

We can tentatively accept the Oct 9 UTC window but will confirm once our security team runs the manifest against our policy. Can you provide sample verification commands and a small dry-run bundle today (no activation) so we can validate signatures and artifact structure?

Hi Tim —

Great questions. Answers and concrete artifacts attached. I've included a digest-checksums.txt file (SHA256 + MD5) and an expanded signing-instructions.pdf. Short answers inline and then the commands below.

1) Verification: we sign the artifact bundle with an RSA 4096 key and also publish a cosign attestation (predicate) that your verifier can evaluate. That gives you both a raw signature and an embedded provenance statement. We will provide an RSA public key fingerprint and cosign signing key ID in the push email.

2) Key rotation: signing keys are rotated per-major-release. For emergency hotfix bundles we use a short-lived envelope key; the manifest includes the envelope key_id and expiry UTC timestamp. We can include the full certificate chain if you require HSM verification.

3) Transport: we can produce a tar.gz and ship on encrypted physical media (AES-256) for your SFTP drop box. Format: signed-runtime-20281009.tar.gz.

4) Rollback: the operator rollback sequence is intentionally simple — revert symlink, restart service, and verify healthcheck. Exact commands we recommend (these will be included in the operator runbook attachment):

- Verify checksum: sha256sum signed-runtime-20281009.tar.gz | grep <expected-sha256>
- Verify signature: openssl dgst -sha256 -verify public_key.pem -signature signed-runtime.sig signed-runtime-20281009.tar.gz
- Extract to /opt/runtime-staged; run smoke test script ./smokecheck.sh
- Promote: ln -sfn /opt/runtime-staged /opt/runtime-current && systemctl restart inference.service
- Rollback (if promotion fails): ln -sfn /opt/runtime-prev /opt/runtime-current && systemctl restart inference.service

Attachment notes: digest-checksums.txt includes SHA256 and MD5 for legacy reasons; signing-instructions.pdf contains cosign and openssl samples plus the public key fingerprint. artifact-manifest.yml shows envelope_key_id: kenv-87af and expiry: 2028-10-16T00:00:00Z.

We will push a dry-run bundle to your staging SFTP by 2028-10-05 17:00 UTC for your team to validate. If the dry-run verifies cleanly we will proceed with the physical media drop on Oct 9 in the proposed window.

Let me know if you want us to provide a temporary test cert for your FIPS path or if your team prefers we integrate with your HSM directly.

-David
David Kim
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
